docs.title: Differences from generate-capture
docs.text:
Feature generate-capture generate-tui-simulation Requires live NetBox Yes (demo profile) No — uses fixture data Output format Markdown + JSON artifacts JSON manifest + SVGs Captures CLI command output TUI visual states State control Command argv Predefined state fixtures in tui_simulation.py

The simulation fixtures and theme/state lists are defined in netbox_cli/tui_simulation.py.

docs.title: IDE support
docs.text: All four packages — netbox_sdk, netbox_cli, netbox_tui, and netbox_mcp — ship a PEP 561 py.typed marker and are included in the wheel's package-data. Editors that read PEP 561 (VS Code via Pylance, PyCharm, Pyright on the command line) resolve types from an installed netbox-sdk without extra configuration.

docs.title: VS Code
docs.text:
The repository commits a minimal workspace under .vscode/ so a fresh clone gets a working IDE on first open. When VS Code prompts to install the recommended extensions, accept:

  • ms-python.python
  • ms-python.vscode-pylance
  • charliermarsh.ruff

.vscode/settings.json pins the interpreter to ${workspaceFolder}/.venv/bin/python, turns on Pylance indexing and import completions, and runs Ruff as the formatter on save. python.analysis.typeCheckingMode is set to basic to match the [tool.pyright] block in pyproject.toml, so the live diagnostics in your editor agree with the pre-commit gate.

docs.title: Type checking gates
docs.text:
Two type checkers run from the same source tree, at the same basic level:

  • ty (Astral) — used by ty-check in pre-commit and CI; fast feedback on the SDK plus the CLI/TUI/MCP packages.
  • pyright (Pylance-compatible) — used by pyright-check in pre-commit so what Pylance shows in VS Code matches what fails in commit hooks.

To run them manually:

uv run ty check netbox_sdk netbox_cli netbox_tui netbox_mcp tests
uv run pyright netbox_sdk netbox_cli netbox_tui netbox_mcp

Both gates must pass before commit. The pyright-check hook sits next to ty-check in .pre-commit-config.yaml; uv run pre-commit run --all-files exercises both.

docs.title: Excluded paths
docs.text:
Generated and bundled code is excluded from both checkers to keep them fast and to avoid noise from generated bindings:

  • netbox_sdk/models/**
  • netbox_sdk/typed_versions/**
  • tests/** (for pyright; ty checks tests but silences all via its overrides block)

docs.title: Rule severity
docs.text:
[tool.pyright] downgrades a small set of rules to warning so they surface in the editor without failing the pre-commit gate. These mirror what ty already silences plus the pyright analogs that surfaced on existing code:

  • reportAttributeAccessIssue
  • reportArgumentType
  • reportAssignmentType
  • reportRedeclaration
  • reportInvalidTypeArguments

Fixing the underlying typing debt is a separate concern from making the IDE work; addressing those warnings should not happen as a side effect of unrelated changes.

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text:
If you install netbox-sdk from PyPI into another project, Pylance picks up the bundled type hints automatically — there is nothing to enable in the consuming repository. The wheel includes:

  • netbox_sdk/py.typed
  • netbox_cli/py.typed
  • netbox_tui/py.typed
  • netbox_mcp/py.typed

Hovering NetBoxApiClient, api(), or typed_api() in a consumer codebase resolves to the real types.

docs.title: Integration with proxbox-api
docs.text:
This page shows exactly how proxbox-api consumes netbox-sdk to connect Proxmox inventory data to NetBox objects. All code examples are drawn from the real proxbox-api source tree.

Source repositories

  • proxbox_api/session/netbox.py — session factory and FastAPI dependency providers
  • proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py — REST helper layer (primary production path)
  • proxbox_api/netbox_sdk_helpers.py — facade-level helpers (to_dict, ensure_record)
  • proxbox_api/netbox_compat.py — legacy sync compatibility wrappers
  • proxbox_api/e2e/session.py — E2E test client (cache disabled)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
proxbox-api is a FastAPI service that reads Proxmox inventory (nodes, VMs, clusters) and creates or updates matching objects in NetBox. netbox-sdk is the sole library used to communicate with NetBox.

flowchart LR
    ROUTE["FastAPI Route\nDependency injection"]
    SESSION["session/netbox.py\nSession factory"]
    CLIENT["NetBoxApiClient\nnetbox_sdk/client.py"]
    NB["NetBox REST API\n:443"]

    ROUTE -->|"Depends(get_netbox_async_session)"| SESSION
    SESSION -->|"Api(client=NetBoxApiClient(cfg))"| CLIENT
    CLIENT -->|"HTTPS + auth + cache"| NB

docs.title: Session Factory Pattern
docs.text: The session factory lives in proxbox_api/session/netbox.py. It builds an Api facade from a NetBoxEndpoint record stored in the local SQLite database.

docs.title: Config from Database Endpoint
docs.text:
proxbox_api/session/netbox.py
from netbox_sdk.client import NetBoxApiClient
from netbox_sdk.config import Config
from netbox_sdk.facade import Api
from netbox_sdk.schema import build_schema_index

def netbox_config_from_endpoint(endpoint: NetBoxEndpoint) -> Config:
    """Build netbox-sdk Config from a stored NetBox endpoint (v1 or v2 tokens)."""
    tv = (endpoint.token_version or "v1").strip().lower()
    if tv not in ("v1", "v2"):
        raise ProxboxException(
            message="Invalid token version in stored endpoint",
            detail=f"Token version must be 'v1' or 'v2', got '{tv}'",
        )
    decrypted_key = endpoint.get_decrypted_token_key()
    key = decrypted_key.strip() if decrypted_key else None
    if tv == "v1":
        key = None
    return Config(
        base_url=endpoint.url,
        token_version=tv,
        token_key=key,
        token_secret=endpoint.get_decrypted_token(),
        timeout=_resolve_netbox_timeout(),   # PROXBOX_NETBOX_TIMEOUT env var
        ssl_verify=endpoint.verify_ssl,
    )

The get_decrypted_token() call decrypts the token from the SQLite database using Fernet encryption. Credentials never travel in plaintext.

docs.title: LRU-Cached Api Construction
docs.text:
Api instances are cached per unique endpoint configuration, so multiple requests within the same process reuse the same NetBoxApiClient (and its pooled aiohttp.ClientSession):

proxbox_api/session/netbox.py
@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
def _cached_netbox_api(
    base_url: str,
    token_version: str,
    token_key: str | None,
    token_secret: str | None,
    timeout: float,
    ssl_verify: bool,
) -> Api:
    cfg = Config(
        base_url=base_url,
        token_version=token_version,
        token_key=token_key,
        token_secret=token_secret,
        timeout=timeout,
        ssl_verify=ssl_verify,
    )
    return Api(
        client=NetBoxApiClient(cfg),
        schema=build_schema_index(version="4.5"),
    )

The cache key uses only primitive types (strings, floats, bools) — functools.lru_cache requires hashable arguments.

docs.title: FastAPI Dependency Injection
docs.text:
proxbox_api/session/netbox.py
async def get_netbox_async_session(
    database_session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_session),
    netbox_id: int | None = None,
) -> Api:
    """Get NetBox API session from database endpoint."""
    result = await database_session.exec(
        select(NetBoxEndpoint).order_by(NetBoxEndpoint.id)
    )
    netbox_endpoint = result.first()
    return netbox_api_from_endpoint(netbox_endpoint)


# Type alias used throughout route modules
NetBoxAsyncSessionDep = Annotated[object, Depends(get_netbox_async_session)]

Route handlers declare nb: NetBoxAsyncSessionDep to receive a ready Api instance:

proxbox_api/routes (pattern)
@router.get("/status")
async def netbox_status(nb: NetBoxAsyncSessionDep):
    return await check_netbox_connection(nb)

Session lifecycle in proxbox-api:

sequenceDiagram
    participant Route as FastAPI Route
    participant Dep as get_netbox_async_session
    participant DB as SQLite Database
    participant Cache as lru_cache
    participant SDK as netbox_sdk

    Route->>Dep: Depends() — called per request
    Dep->>DB: SELECT NetBoxEndpoint ORDER BY id
    DB-->>Dep: endpoint record
    Dep->>Cache: _cached_netbox_api(base_url, token_version, ...)
    alt Cache HIT
        Cache-->>Dep: existing Api instance
    else Cache MISS
        Cache->>SDK: Api(client=NetBoxApiClient(Config(...)))
        SDK-->>Cache: Api instance
        Cache-->>Dep: Api instance
    end
    Dep-->>Route: Api (nb)

docs.title: Two API Access Patterns
docs.text:
proxbox-api uses netbox-sdk in two distinct ways depending on the call site:

Facade PatternDirect REST Pattern

The facade pattern uses attribute-chain navigation to reach typed endpoints, then calls CRUD methods. This is the legacy path used in netbox_compat.py and netbox_sdk_helpers.py.

proxbox_api/netbox_sdk_helpers.py
async def ensure_record(endpoint, lookup, payload) -> NetBoxRecord:
    """Get a record by lookup fields or create it when missing."""
    # Navigate to the endpoint and call .get() with keyword filters
    record = await endpoint.get(**lookup)
    if record:
        return record
    # Create if not found
    return await endpoint.create(payload)


async def ensure_tag(nb, *, name, slug, color, description) -> TagLike:
    """Get or create a NetBox tag."""
    return await ensure_record(
        nb.extras.tags,          # ← attribute navigation: Api → App → Endpoint
        {"slug": slug},
        {"name": name, "slug": slug, "color": color, "description": description},
    )
proxbox_api/netbox_compat.py
# Async iteration over all virtual machines
async for item in nb.virtualization.virtual_machines.all():
    results.append(to_dict(item))

# Lookup by keyword args
vm = await nb.virtualization.virtual_machines.get(name="myvm")

When to use: When the existing facade navigation covers your resource, or when you need full Record dirty tracking and .save().

The direct REST pattern bypasses the facade and calls api.client.request() directly. This is the primary production path in proxbox-api — used in netbox_rest.py for all sync operations.

proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py
async def rest_list_async(nb, path, *, query=None) -> list[RestRecord]:
    response = await nb.client.request("GET", normalized_path, query=query)
    payload = _extract_payload(response)
    results = payload.get("results", [])
    return [RestRecord(nb, path, item) for item in results]


async def rest_create_async(nb, path, payload) -> RestRecord:
    response = await nb.client.request("POST", path, payload=payload)
    body = _extract_payload(response)
    return RestRecord(nb, path, body)

When to use: When you need full control over the request, when the resource isn't covered by the facade schema, or when you're implementing reconciliation logic.

Trade-off summary:

Aspect Facade Pattern Direct REST Pattern Navigation Attribute-chain (nb.dcim.devices) Explicit path string (/api/dcim/devices/) Schema dependency Requires resource in SchemaIndex None — any path Pagination Auto-pagination via RecordSet Manual (proxbox-api adds its own) Dirty tracking Built into Record.save() RestRecord._dirty_fields Validation PyNetBox-style duck-typing Pydantic schema validation optional

docs.title: REST Helper Layer
docs.text: proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py wraps api.client.request() with a complete production-grade HTTP layer: in-memory GET cache, concurrency control, retry with exponential backoff, and response normalization.

docs.title: RestRecord
docs.text:
RestRecord is a minimal mutable record wrapper for direct REST responses. It mirrors the facade Record interface so downstream code can treat both interchangeably:

proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py
class RestRecord:
    def __init__(self, api, list_path, values: dict) -> None:
        self._api = api
        self._list_path = list_path
        self._data = dict(values)
        self._dirty_fields: set[str] = set()

    def __setattr__(self, name, value):
        if name in {"_api", "_list_path", "_data", "_dirty_fields"}:
            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
        else:
            self._data[name] = value
            self._dirty_fields.add(name)    # ← dirty tracking

    async def save(self) -> RestRecord:
        payload = {f: self._data[f] for f in self._dirty_fields if f in self._data}
        response = await self._api.client.request("PATCH", self._detail_path, payload=payload)
        ...

    async def delete(self) -> bool:
        response = await self._api.client.request("DELETE", self._detail_path, expect_json=False)
        ...

docs.title: Core Helpers
docs.text: Function Method Description rest_list_async(nb, path, query=...) GET Returns list[RestRecord], with caching rest_first_async(nb, path, query=...) GET Returns first RestRecord or None rest_create_async(nb, path, payload) POST Creates and returns RestRecord rest_patch_async(nb, path, id, payload) PATCH Updates record by ID rest_ensure_async(nb, path, lookup=..., payload=...) GET+POST Get-or-create with duplicate recovery rest_reconcile_async(nb, path, lookup=..., payload=..., schema=...) GET+POST+PATCH Full diff and patch reconciliation rest_bulk_create_async(nb, path, payloads) POST Bulk create rest_bulk_reconcile_async(...) GET+POST+PATCH Batch reconciliation

docs.title: rest_ensure_async — Get-or-Create
docs.text:
proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py
async def rest_ensure_async(nb, path, *, lookup, payload) -> RestRecord:
    # Try multiple candidate lookups (by slug, name, model, etc.)
    for candidate in _candidate_reuse_lookups(lookup, payload):
        existing = await rest_first_async(nb, path, query={**candidate, "limit": 2})
        if existing:
            return existing

    # Create if not found
    try:
        return await rest_create_async(nb, path, payload)
    except ProxboxException as error:
        # Recover from race-condition duplicate errors
        if _is_duplicate_error(error.detail):
            for candidate in _candidate_reuse_lookups(lookup, payload):
                retry = await rest_first_async(nb, path, query={**candidate, "limit": 2})
                if retry:
                    return retry
        raise

Decision flow:

flowchart TD
    START["rest_ensure_async(nb, path, lookup, payload)"]
    CANDIDATES["Build lookup candidates\n(slug, name, model, compound keys)"]
    GET["GET with candidate filter\nrest_first_async()"]
    FOUND{"Record found?"}
    CREATE["POST create record\nrest_create_async()"]
    DUPERR{"Duplicate error?\n(race condition)"}
    RETRY["Retry GET — concurrent\nrequest created it first"]
    RAISE["Re-raise error"]
    RETURN["Return RestRecord"]

    START --> CANDIDATES --> GET --> FOUND
    FOUND -->|Yes| RETURN
    FOUND -->|No| CREATE
    CREATE --> DUPERR
    DUPERR -->|Yes| RETRY --> RETURN
    DUPERR -->|No| RAISE

docs.title: rest_reconcile_async — Diff and Patch
docs.text:
rest_reconcile_async is the highest-level helper. It finds an existing record, computes a diff against the desired payload, and only issues a PATCH if fields diverge:

proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py (simplified)
async def rest_reconcile_async(nb, path, *, lookup, payload, schema, current_normalizer, ...):
    desired_model = schema.model_validate(payload)
    desired_payload = desired_model.model_dump(exclude_none=True, by_alias=True)

    existing = await _find_existing(nb, path, lookup, desired_payload)
    if existing is None:
        return await rest_create_async(nb, path, desired_payload)

    # Compute diff
    current_payload = schema.model_validate(current_normalizer(existing.serialize())).model_dump(...)
    patch_payload = {k: v for k, v in desired_payload.items() if current_payload.get(k) != v}

    if patch_payload:
        for field, value in patch_payload.items():
            setattr(existing, field, value)
        await existing.save()    # PATCH only changed fields

    return existing

docs.title: Semaphore-Based Rate Limiting
docs.text:
All REST helpers share a single asyncio.Semaphore to cap concurrent NetBox requests. The default is 1 to avoid exhausting NetBox's PostgreSQL connection pool:

proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py
_netbox_request_semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None

def _get_netbox_semaphore() -> asyncio.Semaphore:
    global _netbox_request_semaphore
    if _netbox_request_semaphore is None:
        _netbox_request_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(_resolve_netbox_max_concurrent())
    return _netbox_request_semaphore

# In every REST helper:
async with semaphore:
    return await _do_request()
Variable Default Description PROXBOX_NETBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT 1 Semaphore limit — increase only if NetBox has sufficient DB pool capacity PROXBOX_NETBOX_MAX_RETRIES 5 Max retry attempts per request PROXBOX_NETBOX_RETRY_DELAY 2.0 Base retry delay in seconds PROXBOX_NETBOX_GET_CACHE_TTL 60.0 In-memory GET cache TTL (set to 0 to disable) PROXBOX_NETBOX_GET_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES 4096 Max cached GET responses PROXBOX_NETBOX_GET_CACHE_MAX_BYTES 50 MB Max total cache size

docs.title: In-Memory GET Cache
docs.text:
netbox_rest.py maintains its own module-level GET cache that sits in front of the SDK's filesystem cache. This avoids repeated disk reads within a single sync run:

proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py (simplified)
_netbox_get_cache: dict[tuple[int, str, str], tuple[float, int, list[dict]]] = {}
# Key: (id(api), normalized_path, serialized_query)
# Value: (cached_at: float, size_bytes: int, records: list[dict])

Cache keys use id(api) to scope cached results to a specific Api instance, preventing cross-endpoint contamination. GET cache entries are invalidated after any POST/PATCH/DELETE on the same path.

docs.title: Retry with Exponential Backoff
docs.text:
Every REST helper wraps its _do_request() call in a retry loop with exponential backoff and jitter:

proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py
for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
    async with semaphore:
        try:
            return await _do_request()
        except Exception as e:
            if attempt == max_retries or not _is_transient_netbox_error(e):
                raise
            delay = _compute_retry_delay(base_delay, attempt, e)
            logger.warning(
                "NetBox request failed (attempt %s/%s), retrying in %ss: %s",
                attempt + 1, max_retries + 1, delay, str(e)[:200],
            )
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)


def _compute_retry_delay(base_delay: float, attempt: int, error: Exception) -> float:
    exponential_delay = base_delay * (2 ** attempt)
    if _is_connection_refused_error(error):
        exponential_delay = max(exponential_delay, 10.0)
    if _is_netbox_overwhelmed_error(error):
        exponential_delay = max(exponential_delay, 30.0)  # DB pool saturated
    return exponential_delay + random.uniform(0, exponential_delay * 0.5)  # jitter

Retry backoff progression (default: base_delay=2.0s):

Attempt Min delay Max delay 1 2.0 s 3.0 s 2 4.0 s 6.0 s 3 8.0 s 12.0 s 4 16.0 s 24.0 s 5 32.0 s 48.0 s

NetBox overwhelmed detection

When NetBox returns an error consistent with PostgreSQL pool exhaustion (e.g., too many connections, connection pool), the minimum delay jumps to 30 seconds to give the database time to recover.

docs.title: Compatibility Wrappers
docs.text:
proxbox_api/netbox_compat.py provides sync wrappers over the async facade for legacy code paths that predate proxbox-api's async rewrite. Each wrapper maps an endpoint_getter string to a facade attribute path and bridges sync-to-async via a thread:

proxbox_api/netbox_compat.py
class _BaseCompat:
    endpoint_getter: str = ""   # e.g. "virtualization.virtual_machines"

    @classmethod
    def _endpoint(cls, nb):
        endpoint = nb
        for piece in cls.endpoint_getter.split("."):
            endpoint = getattr(endpoint, piece)
        return endpoint

    def all(self) -> list[dict]:
        async def _op():
            endpoint = self._endpoint(self._nb())
            results = []
            async for item in endpoint.all():
                results.append(to_dict(item))
            return results
        return _run(_op())      # runs coroutine in a thread if inside event loop


class Tags(_BaseCompat):
    endpoint_getter = "extras.tags"

class VirtualMachine(_BaseCompat):
    endpoint_getter = "virtualization.virtual_machines"

    @staticmethod
    def map_status(proxmox_status: str) -> str:
        return ProxmoxToNetBoxVMStatus.from_proxmox(proxmox_status)

Available wrappers:

Class endpoint_getter Resource Tags extras.tags NetBox tags CustomField extras.custom_fields Custom fields ClusterType virtualization.cluster_types Cluster types Cluster virtualization.clusters Clusters Site dcim.sites Sites DeviceRole dcim.device_roles Device roles Manufacturer dcim.manufacturers Manufacturers DeviceType dcim.device_types Device types Device dcim.devices Devices Interface dcim.interfaces Physical interfaces VMInterface virtualization.interfaces VM interfaces IPAddress ipam.ip_addresses IP addresses VirtualMachine virtualization.virtual_machines Virtual machines

Migration path

New proxbox-api code uses rest_ensure_async / rest_reconcile_async from netbox_rest.py instead of these wrappers. The wrappers exist for backward compatibility with older routes that predate the REST helper layer.

docs.title: Response Validation
docs.text:
_extract_payload() validates every response and normalizes error details:

proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py
def _extract_payload(response: ApiResponse) -> object:
    if response.status < 200 or response.status >= 300:
        detail = response.text
        try:
            payload = response.json()
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            payload = None

        if isinstance(payload, dict):
            detail = str(payload.get("detail") or payload.get("message") or detail)
        elif isinstance(payload, list):
            parts = [str(item) for item in payload if item]
            if parts:
                detail = "; ".join(parts)

        raise ProxboxException(
            message="NetBox REST request failed",
            detail=detail,
        )
    return response.json() if response.text else None

docs.title: Error Classification
docs.text:
_handle_netbox_error() distinguishes transient failures (connection refused, timeout, DNS) from permanent ones and logs at different levels:

proxbox_api/netbox_rest.py
def _handle_netbox_error(error, operation):
    if _is_transient_netbox_error(error):
        logger.warning("Transient NetBox error during %s: %s", operation, error)
    else:
        logger.error("NetBox error during %s: %s", operation, error)

    if _is_netbox_overwhelmed_error(error):
        raise ProxboxException(
            message="NetBox is overwhelmed. Please retry in a few moments.",
            detail=f"{operation} failed: {error}",
        )
    raise ProxboxException(message=f"NetBox {operation} failed", detail=str(error))

docs.title: E2E Testing Pattern
docs.text:
proxbox-api's end-to-end tests use a E2ENetBoxApiClient subclass that disables the SDK's filesystem cache by returning None from _cache_policy(). This ensures tests always see live responses rather than cached state:

proxbox_api/e2e/session.py
from netbox_sdk.client import NetBoxApiClient
from netbox_sdk.facade import Api

class E2ENetBoxApiClient(NetBoxApiClient):
    """NetBox client with HTTP caching disabled for E2E test stability."""

    def _cache_policy(self, *, method, path, query=None, payload=None):
        return None   # Always bypass SDK filesystem cache


async def create_netbox_e2e_session(base_url: str, token: str) -> Api:
    config = Config(
        base_url=base_url,
        token_secret=token,
        token_version="v1",
    )
    client = E2ENetBoxApiClient(config)
    return Api(client=client)

Cache isolation in tests

The E2ENetBoxApiClient subclass is the recommended pattern for any integration test that needs to avoid cross-test cache contamination. The SDK's _cache_policy() method is intentionally designed to be overridable.

docs.title: Package integration
docs.text: This document describes how the installable artifact, import paths, and subsystems fit together.

docs.title: PyPI project and optional extras
docs.text:
The primary PyPI project is netbox-sdk (see pyproject.toml). The same distribution ships three top-level packages:

Import package Role Typical install netbox_sdk REST client, config, schema, services, typed API pip install netbox-sdk netbox_cli Typer nbx CLI pip install 'netbox-sdk[cli]' netbox_tui Textual TUIs pip install 'netbox-sdk[tui]'

Use pip install 'netbox-sdk[all]' for CLI + TUI + demo tooling.

For a reproducible install from the default PyPI index, pin with == and the PEP 440 final or post-release version in docs/snippets/published-package-version.txt (see Installation). The separate docs/snippets/package-version.txt value identifies the in-tree source candidate and TestPyPI artifacts; prerelease, development, and local versions do not publish to the default index.

Release-candidate tags are pushed directly with the exact v*rc* version and publish only to TestPyPI. Final and post releases reach PyPI only from a published GitHub Release. The publishing workflow accepts a closed local set of exactly one package/version-matched wheel and one sdist, captures it before network-installed smoke dependencies run, and gives each registry only a fresh validator-approved upload directory. Before production upload it verifies both the complete TestPyPI set and PyPI's current exact filename/hash set, staging only missing PyPI files so partial uploads resume safely without --skip-existing. The Twine step revalidates the approved filename/digest manifest, and a bounded final check requires PyPI to expose exactly the local wheel/sdist filenames and hashes. Registry jobs install only the audited, locked publish dependency group.

docs.title: Public SDK surface
docs.text:
Stable symbols for library use are exported from netbox_sdk (see netbox_sdk/__init__.py), including:

  • NetBoxApiClient, ApiResponse, ConnectionProbe, RequestError
  • Config, load_profile_config, save_config, and related profile helpers
  • SchemaIndex, load_openapi_schema, build_schema_index
  • ResolvedRequest, resolve_dynamic_request, run_dynamic_command
  • Typed facade (api, typed_api, …) and version support types

Everything outside that __all__ is considered internal unless documented otherwise.

flowchart TB

docs.title: Allowed import edges
docs.text: From May import Notes netbox_sdk stdlib + declared deps only Must not import netbox_cli or netbox_tui. netbox_cli netbox_sdk, then netbox_tui only via lazy helpers (support.load_tui_callables) Entry: netbox_cli:main → nbx. netbox_tui netbox_sdk Receives NetBoxApiClient and SchemaIndex from the caller or CLI.

docs.title: In-process runtime state (netbox_cli.runtime)
docs.text: netbox_cli.runtime holds _RUNTIME_CONFIGS, _cache_profile, _get_client, _get_registration_index, _get_runtime_index, and related helpers. _get_registration_index() builds the network-free command tree from the selected bundled schema, while _get_runtime_index() honors explicit version overrides or detects the configured instance release line for execution. Demo token refresh updates the cached profile via _cache_profile so the CLI process stays consistent without the SDK client importing Typer.

docs.title: CLI command registration
docs.text: Commands are registered on the root Typer app in netbox_cli/__init__.py. Dynamic OpenAPI commands are built in netbox_cli/dynamic.py; _runtime_get_client / _runtime_get_index resolve through netbox_cli.runtime at call time so tests can patch those factories.

docs.title: Entry point
docs.text:
Console script nbx maps to netbox_cli:main.

See also: Architecture, Design principles.

docs.title: SDK Internals
docs.text: This page explains how netbox_sdk works under the hood — the HTTP client lifecycle, config and profile system, OpenAPI schema indexing, the facade object hierarchy, versioned typed clients, filesystem HTTP cache, and the services layer.

docs.title: NetBoxApiClient Request Lifecycle
docs.text:
NetBoxApiClient in netbox_sdk/client.py is the central async HTTP client. Every request passes through the same pipeline regardless of which API layer (raw, facade, or typed) initiated it.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as Caller code
    participant Client as NetBoxApiClient
    participant Cache as HttpCacheStore
    participant Session as aiohttp.ClientSession
    participant NB as NetBox API

    Caller->>Client: request("GET", "/api/dcim/devices/", query={...})
    Client->>Client: _normalize_request_path() — SSRF guard
    Client->>Client: authorization_header_value() — build auth header
    Client->>Client: _cache_policy() — determine TTL policy
    Client->>Cache: load(cache_key)
    alt Cache FRESH (within TTL)
        Cache-->>Client: CacheEntry
        Client-->>Caller: ApiResponse (X-NBX-Cache: HIT)
    else Cache STALE or MISS
        alt Stale entry exists
            Client->>Client: add If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since headers
        end
        Client->>Client: _get_session() — lazy aiohttp session
        Client->>Session: session.request(GET, url, ...)
        Session->>NB: HTTPS GET
        NB-->>Session: 200 {...} or 304 Not Modified
        Session-->>Client: raw response
        alt 401/403 with v2 token
            Client->>Session: retry with Token fallback header
        end
        Client->>Cache: save(key, entry, policy)
        Client-->>Caller: ApiResponse
    end

docs.title: Lazy Session Creation
docs.text:
The aiohttp.ClientSession is created on the first request and reused for all subsequent calls. A double-check lock pattern handles event-loop affinity:

netbox_sdk/client.py
async def _get_session(self) -> aiohttp.ClientSession:
    current_loop_id = id(asyncio.get_running_loop())

    # Fast path: session already valid for this loop — no lock needed
    if (
        self._session is not None
        and not self._session_closed()
        and self._session_loop_id == current_loop_id
    ):
        return self._session

    async with self._get_lock():
        # Re-check under lock in case another coroutine just created the session
        if self._session is None or session_closed or self._session_loop_id != current_loop_id:
            ...
            self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=..., connector=...)
            self._session_loop_id = current_loop_id
        return self._session

docs.title: SSRF Protection
docs.text:
All request paths pass through _normalize_request_path(), which rejects absolute URLs, query strings, and fragments embedded in the path argument:

netbox_sdk/client.py
def _normalize_request_path(self, path: str) -> str:
    parsed = urlsplit(path.strip())
    if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc:
        raise ValueError("Request path must be relative to the configured NetBox base URL")
    if parsed.query or parsed.fragment:
        raise ValueError("Request path must not include query parameters or fragments")
    return parsed.path if parsed.path.startswith("/") else f"/{parsed.path}"

docs.title: v2-to-v1 Token Fallback
docs.text:
When a v2 nbt_ token receives a 401/403 with "invalid v2 token" in the body, the client retries transparently with a Token <secret> v1 header:

netbox_sdk/client.py
def _should_retry_with_v1(self, response: ApiResponse) -> bool:
    if self.config.token_version != "v2" or not self.config.token_secret:
        return False
    if response.status not in {401, 403}:
        return False
    return "invalid v2 token" in response.text.lower()

docs.title: Config and Profile System
docs.text: Config in netbox_sdk/config.py is a Pydantic model that normalizes and validates connection parameters before passing them to NetBoxApiClient.

docs.title: Fields and Validators
docs.text:
Field Type Description base_url str \| None NetBox base URL — normalized to http:// or https:// only token_version str "v1" (legacy Token) or "v2" (nbt_ bearer) token_key str \| None v2 token key prefix (before .) token_secret str \| None Token value — CR/LF/null stripped to prevent header injection timeout float HTTP timeout in seconds (default: 30.0) ssl_verify bool TLS certificate verification (default: True) demo_username str \| None Username for demo profile auto-login demo_password str \| None Password for demo profile auto-login

Validators strip control characters from token values and reject URLs with embedded credentials.

docs.title: Multi-Profile Persistence
docs.text:
Profiles are stored as {"profiles": {"default": {...}, "demo": {...}}} in ~/.config/netbox-sdk/config.json with 0o600 permissions (owner read/write only):

netbox_sdk/config.py (pattern)
# Load the active profile
config = load_profile_config(profile="default")

# Save updated credentials
save_config(config, profile="default")

docs.title: Environment Variable Override
docs.text:
Variable Config field NETBOX_URL base_url NETBOX_TOKEN_KEY token_key NETBOX_TOKEN_SECRET token_secret NETBOX_SSL_VERIFY ssl_verify DEMO_USERNAME demo_username DEMO_PASSWORD demo_password

Environment variables take precedence over the profile config file.

docs.title: SchemaIndex (OpenAPI Parsing)
docs.text:
SchemaIndex in netbox_sdk/schema.py parses the bundled OpenAPI JSON into an in-memory index optimized for fast group/resource/operation lookups.

flowchart LR
    JSON["netbox-openapi-4.5.json\n(bundled)"]
    BUILD["SchemaIndex._build()\nparse all paths"]
    OPS["_operations\nlist[Operation]"]
    RPATHS["_resource_paths\ndict[group+resource → ResourcePaths]"]
    GROUPS["groups() → list[str]"]
    RES["resources(group) → list[str]"]
    OPFOR["operations_for(group, resource) → list[Operation]"]
    FILTER["filter_params(group, resource) → list[FilterParam]"]

    JSON --> BUILD
    BUILD --> OPS
    BUILD --> RPATHS
    OPS --> GROUPS
    OPS --> RES
    OPS --> OPFOR
    RPATHS --> FILTER

docs.title: Path Parsing
docs.text:
parse_group_resource() splits any NetBox API path into a (group, resource) tuple:

  • /api/dcim/devices/ → ("dcim", "devices")
  • /api/plugins/my-plugin/widgets/ → ("plugins", "my-plugin/widgets")
  • /api/ipam/ip-addresses/{id}/ → ("ipam", "ip-addresses")

docs.title: Plugin Discovery
docs.text:
enrich_schema_index_with_runtime_resources() is the preferred high-level call: it walks the live /api/plugins/ endpoint, parses each discovered path, and calls add_discovered_resource() on the supplied index. It returns True if the index changed.

from netbox_sdk.plugin_discovery import enrich_schema_index_with_runtime_resources

changed = await enrich_schema_index_with_runtime_resources(schema_index, client)
# True when at least one new resource was registered

For lower-level control, discover_plugin_resource_paths() returns a list of (list_path, detail_path) tuples:

from netbox_sdk.plugin_discovery import discover_plugin_resource_paths

paths = await discover_plugin_resource_paths(client)
# [("/api/plugins/gpon/olts/", "/api/plugins/gpon/olts/{id}/"), ...]

for list_path, detail_path in paths:
    # parse group/resource from list_path and call add_discovered_resource manually
    ...

docs.title: Versioned Bundled Schemas
docs.text:
Versioned OpenAPI schemas ship with the package under netbox_sdk/reference/openapi/. load_openapi_schema() defaults to the NetBox 4.6 schema unless a supported release line is supplied explicitly.

File NetBox Version netbox-openapi.json Legacy compatibility alias netbox-openapi-4.7.json NetBox 4.7 (preview) netbox-openapi-4.6.json NetBox 4.6 netbox-openapi-4.5.json NetBox 4.5 netbox-openapi-4.4.json NetBox 4.4 netbox-openapi-4.3.json NetBox 4.3

docs.title: Release Registry and Shared Resolution
docs.text:
netbox_sdk/versioning.py is the single owner of release-line metadata. Each frozen ReleaseLine record binds a line to its lifecycle status, bundled OpenAPI filename, generated-model module, and typed-client module. Existing constants such as SUPPORTED_NETBOX_VERSIONS and DEFAULT_NETBOX_VERSION are views over this registry; the default is the value returned by latest_stable_line().

netbox_sdk/schema_resolution.py is the single selection policy used by the SDK, CLI, TUI, and MCP surfaces. requested_netbox_version() reads CLI aliases before the supported environment variables. resolve_index() then applies one precedence ladder:

  1. An explicit argument or CLI/environment pin selects that bundled line.
  2. A connected supported instance selects its matching bundled line.
  3. A connected unsupported instance supplies /api/schema/ dynamically.
  4. Detection, fetch, or document failures use the default bundled line.

bundled_index() caches the parsed base index per process, but every call returns SchemaIndex.clone(). Runtime plugin discoveries therefore remain local to one CLI, TUI, facade, or MCP session.

docs.title: Facade Object Hierarchy
docs.text:
netbox_sdk/facade.py provides a PyNetBox-compatible async API. The api() factory builds the root Api object; subsequent attribute accesses create App → Endpoint → Record / RecordSet objects.

flowchart TB
    APIFN["api(url, token)\nfactory function"]
    API["Api\n.client · .schema · .dcim · .ipam · …"]
    APP["App('dcim')\n__getattr__ → Endpoint"]
    ENDPOINT["Endpoint('devices')\n.all() · .filter() · .get() · .create()"]
    RECORDSET["RecordSet\nasync iterator · auto-pagination"]
    RECORD["Record\nattribute access · dirty tracking\n.save() · .delete()"]

    APIFN --> API
    API -->|".dcim"| APP
    APP -->|".devices"| ENDPOINT
    ENDPOINT -->|".all()"| RECORDSET
    RECORDSET -->|"async for item in …"| RECORD
    ENDPOINT -->|".get(id)"| RECORD
    ENDPOINT -->|".create(payload)"| RECORD

docs.title: CRUD Operations
docs.text:
netbox_sdk/facade.py (usage)
nb = api("https://netbox.example.com", token="...")

# List all — async iteration with auto-pagination
async for device in nb.dcim.devices.all():
    print(device.name, device.status)

# Filter with query params
records = nb.dcim.devices.filter(site="nyc-dc1", status="active")
async for device in records:
    print(device)

# Get single by ID
device = await nb.dcim.devices.get(42)

# Create
tag = await nb.extras.tags.create({
    "name": "proxmox",
    "slug": "proxmox",
    "color": "ff5722",
})

# Get or create via facade (using lookup keywords)
result = await nb.extras.tags.get(slug="proxmox")

docs.title: Record Dirty Tracking
docs.text:
Record captures a snapshot of field values at creation time. Mutating a field adds it to a _updates dict; calling .save() sends only the changed fields as a PATCH:

netbox_sdk/facade.py (usage)
device = await nb.dcim.devices.get(42)
device.status = "offline"          # marks "status" dirty
device.comments = "decommissioned" # marks "comments" dirty
await device.save()                 # PATCH {status, comments} only

docs.title: Specialized Record Types
docs.text: Type Resource Extras TraceableRecord DCIM interfaces, power ports, etc. .trace() → cable trace result PathableRecord Circuit terminations .paths() → path list DeviceRecord dcim.devices .render_config(), .napalm()

docs.title: Typed API (Versioned Clients)
docs.text:
typed_api() in netbox_sdk/typed_api.py returns a version-specific typed client backed by generated Pydantic models for full IDE completion and runtime validation.

Usage
from netbox_sdk import typed_api

nb = typed_api("https://netbox.example.com", token="...", netbox_version="4.5")

# Full Pydantic validation on request and response
device = await nb.dcim.devices.retrieve(42)
device.name    # str — IDE knows the type
device.status  # DeviceStatus enum

docs.title: Version Selection
docs.text:
The netbox_version argument maps to a dynamically imported module:

netbox_sdk/typed_api.py (simplified)
def typed_api(url, token, *, netbox_version):
    normalized = normalize_netbox_version(netbox_version)
    module = import_module(release_line(normalized).typed_module)
    return module.build_api(url, token)

Overloaded return types provide IDE completion per version:

netbox_sdk/typed_api.py
@overload
def typed_api(url: str, token: str | None = None, *, netbox_version: Literal["4.6"]) -> TypedApiV4_6: ...
@overload
def typed_api(url: str, token: str | None = None, *, netbox_version: Literal["4.5"]) -> TypedApiV4_5: ...
@overload
def typed_api(url: str, token: str | None = None, *, netbox_version: Literal["4.4"]) -> TypedApiV4_4: ...
@overload
def typed_api(url: str, token: str | None = None, *, netbox_version: Literal["4.3"]) -> TypedApiV4_3: ...

docs.title: HTTP Cache
docs.text:
HttpCacheStore in netbox_sdk/http_cache.py provides a filesystem-backed JSON cache stored under ~/.config/netbox-sdk/http-cache/.

flowchart TD
    REQ["Incoming GET request"]
    KEY["build_cache_key()\nSHA-256 of base_url + method + path + query + token fingerprint"]
    LOAD["HttpCacheStore.load(key)"]
    FRESH{"Entry exists\nand is fresh?"}
    STALE{"Entry exists\nbut stale?"}
    COND["Add If-None-Match /\nIf-Modified-Since headers"]
    HTTP["Make HTTP request"]
    STATUS{"Response status"}
    S304["304 Not Modified\n→ refresh timestamps"]
    S2XX["2xx → save new entry"]
    S5XX["5xx error\n→ serve stale if within\nstale_if_error_until"]
    RETURN["Return ApiResponse\n(X-NBX-Cache header)"]

    REQ --> KEY --> LOAD --> FRESH
    FRESH -->|Yes| RETURN
    FRESH -->|No| STALE
    STALE -->|Yes| COND --> HTTP
    STALE -->|No| HTTP
    HTTP --> STATUS
    STATUS --> S304 --> RETURN
    STATUS --> S2XX --> RETURN
    STATUS --> S5XX --> RETURN

docs.title: Cache Key
docs.text:
Cache keys are SHA-256 fingerprints of the request identity — never raw credentials:

netbox_sdk/http_cache.py
def build_cache_key(*, base_url, method, path, query, authorization) -> str:
    token_fingerprint = hashlib.sha256((authorization or "").encode()).hexdigest()
    identity = "\n".join([
        base_url.rstrip("/"),
        method.upper(),
        path,
        urlencode(sorted((query or {}).items()), doseq=True),
        token_fingerprint,
    ])
    return hashlib.sha256(identity.encode()).hexdigest()

docs.title: Header Precedence and Authorization Resolution
docs.text:
Request headers layer from three sources, lowest to highest precedence: persistent_headers (client-wide, e.g. the TUI's active branch or MCP's forwarded-caller override), _scoped_headers (a per-task contextvars.ContextVar set by header_scope()/activate_branch()), and the per-call headers argument. HTTP header names are case-insensitive but a plain dict is not, so _extract_case_insensitive() pops every case variant of a header name (Authorization, authorization, AUTHORIZATION, ...) from a headers dict and returns both explicit-presence state and the matching value, plus the remainder with all variants removed.

_request_impl() and stream_sse() both extract Authorization from each layer separately, before merging them, then choose the highest-precedence layer whose key was present. Presence rather than truthiness is security-critical: headers={"Authorization": ""} and an empty Authorization supplied through header_scope() intentionally select anonymous dispatch and must not fall through to the client's configured, potentially privileged token. When no layer supplies the key, the configured credential is still used; non-empty overrides behave as before. Per-layer extraction also avoids plain-dict iteration-order traps when different casing is used at different precedence levels.

docs.title: Cache Policies
docs.text:
Request type Fresh TTL Stale-if-error TTL GET list (e.g., /api/dcim/devices/) 60 s 300 s GET detail with query 30 s 60 s GET detail without query 15 s 60 s Non-GET (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) Not cached —

Cache files use 0o600 permissions (owner read/write only) to protect token fingerprints.

docs.title: Write Invalidation and Generation Fencing
docs.text:
A non-GET request purges every cached entry for its path (and the containing collection path) via HttpCacheStore.invalidate_path(), keyed by a per-path index file rather than the full cache key — so invalidation is independent of which token, query string, or scope headers produced the cached entry. Invalidation runs after any completed write attempt, regardless of response status, and after an exception raised while issuing or reading the write (connection drop, timeout, malformed response). A non-2xx status is not proof the mutation didn't happen: a plugin or raw endpoint can commit the write server-side and only then fail during post-commit processing (e.g. a 500 from signal/webhook handling after the row was already written), so restricting invalidation to confirmed 2xx responses would leave that committed mutation invisible to the cache and let a verification read serve the stale pre-write entry, encouraging an unsafe duplicate retry. Invalidation failures (e.g. a cache-index filesystem error) are caught and logged as a warning rather than propagated — a cache-maintenance failure must never override a confirmed HTTP outcome, misreporting a successful write as failed or masking the real request exception behind an unrelated OSError. Any such failure — a lock timeout or a plain filesystem error such as a failed unlink or a read-only disk (TimeoutError is itself an OSError subclass, so one except OSError handler covers both) — additionally publishes a per-path cache-unavailable marker: later reads cannot report a HIT from the surviving entry and must complete a real purge before that path can be trusted or populated again.

_invalidate_related_cache() purges each affected path (the exact path, the collection path, and — for bulk writes — each item's own detail path) independently, catching and logging a failure on any single path rather than wrapping the whole batch in one try/except. A write can affect several distinct cache paths, and a failure purging the first one (e.g. a transient lock contention) must never abort the attempt on the rest: skipping the remaining paths after one early failure would leave them — most importantly the containing collection listing — fully cached and able to serve a fresh-looking pre-write hit immediately after the write succeeds, even though the exact path that did fail is logged and known-stale.

A GET that started before a write can still be in flight when that write's invalidate_path() runs. Without a fence, the GET's own save() call — which lands after the invalidation — could resurrect the pre-write response into a fresh cache entry, hiding a successful mutation from the next read for the rest of that entry's TTL. HttpCacheStore closes this race with a per-path generation counter:

  • path_generation(path) returns the path's current generation; the client captures it immediately before issuing a cacheable GET. If coordination times out, its lock-unavailable sentinel is an explicit bypass state: the client neither loads an existing entry nor writes the live response to cache for that request.
  • invalidate_path(path) increments the generation (and clears the key list) instead of deleting the index file outright, so a fence captured before invalidation can still be compared against it afterward.
  • save(..., path=path, expected_generation=<captured>) re-checks the generation under the same per-path lock invalidate_path() uses. If the generation has moved on, the entry is still returned to satisfy the in-flight caller's own request, but neither the entry file nor the index registration is written — the response is never persisted.
  • refresh(..., path=path, expected_generation=<captured>) applies the identical fence to a 304 revalidation. A 304 only confirms that the representation matched the ETag/Last-Modified sent from the pre-write entry; if a concurrent write invalidated the path while the conditional request was in flight, that confirmation is stale and refresh() must not resurrect the purged entry any more than save() would. When the client detects this race directly (the path's generation has moved since the conditional request began, and the response comes back 304), it discards the If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since headers and reissues the request unconditionally before persisting, rather than trusting the untrustworthy 304 at all. The generation passed to that replacement request's own fenced save is captured immediately before the unconditional request is issued, mirroring the capture-before-request pattern used for the very first GET — capturing it only after the replacement response arrives would leave a second race window open: a further concurrent write landing while the unconditional refetch is still in flight would otherwise be adopted as if it were the fence, letting that now-doubly-stale replacement response pass the check and get persisted as a fresh entry. The in-memory cache_entry reference is also dropped at that same point, before the unconditional request is issued — not after it returns. The generation mismatch already proved that entry stale, so it must not survive to be served by either of this request's own stale-if-error fallbacks (the exception handler's stale-if-error return, or _finalize_cached_response()'s stale-on-5xx return) if the unconditional refetch itself then raises or comes back with a server error; clearing it only after a successful refetch would leave both fallbacks able to resurrect the very entry the client just proved could no longer be trusted.

This makes the entry write and index registration atomic with respect to concurrent invalidation, closing the same-race window that a lock alone (serializing writers, not fencing readers against a write that already committed) does not.

docs.title: Action-Endpoint Cross-Resource Invalidation
docs.text:
Most writes only ever affect the path written and its immediate parent collection, which _related_cache_paths()'s default derivation (exact path + _collection_path_for()) already covers. NetBox's "detail action" endpoints — non-CRUD sub-paths registered per (group, resource) in netbox_sdk.facade.DETAIL_ENDPOINT_SPECS, such as available-ips, available-prefixes, and available-vlans — break that assumption: POST /api/ipam/prefixes/{id}/available-ips/ creates IPAddress rows that live under /api/ipam/ip-addresses/, an entirely different collection than the prefix's own path or its parent. The default derivation would purge only /api/ipam/prefixes/{id}/available-ips/ and /api/ipam/prefixes/{id}/, leaving a list cached from /api/ipam/ip-addresses/ before the action stale until it naturally expired.

client.py's module-level _ACTION_CROSS_RESOURCE_CACHE_PATHS maps each known mutating action's trailing path segment (available-ips, available-prefixes, available-vlans) to the extra collection path(s) it actually populates. _trailing_action_name() recognizes the general trailing shape ... / resource / numeric-id / non-numeric-action, so core routes and plugin routes with additional leading namespaces are handled identically. _related_cache_paths() always steps back past both the action and ID to invalidate the resource's true collection, then adds mapped cross-resource collection(s) whenever the written action matches. Read-only actions (napalm, trace, units, elevation, paths) are omitted from the mapping since a GET never stales anything.

Deliberately out of scope: aggregate/derived fields on unrelated resources. This is a path-based cache, not a dependency-aware one. Writing a Device does not invalidate a cached Site, Rack, or DeviceType listing even though NetBox's read-only aggregates (e.g. device_count) on those objects would now be stale — the only cross-resource invalidation this cache performs is the explicit _ACTION_CROSS_RESOURCE_CACHE_PATHS mapping above, for the specific case of a detail action that is known to create rows under an entirely different collection. Extending this to every relationship that carries a derived/aggregate field would require either a full dependency graph across the bundled OpenAPI schema or unconditional store-wide invalidation on every write, both of which defeat the purpose of a filesystem-level HTTP cache for a CLI/SDK client. Callers that need a guaranteed-fresh aggregate field should not rely on a cached read for it.

The per-path index's read-modify-write is serialized by HttpCacheStore._locked_index(). On platforms with fcntl (Linux, macOS), _acquire_flock() polls flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) on the same bounded timeout/poll_interval deadline _portable_lock already uses, raising TimeoutError if the deadline passes rather than calling the unbounded blocking flock(LOCK_EX) form. It retries only contention errors (EAGAIN/EACCES); any other OSError is propagated immediately instead of being hidden behind the full timeout. The polling loops still use synchronous sleeps because same-path writers require wait-then-succeed semantics: dropping a contended save would lose that caller's key from the shared index. NetBoxApiClient therefore awaits every synchronous cache-store operation (path_generation, load, invalidate_path, unavailable marking, refresh, and save) through asyncio.to_thread(). A held cache lock can delay that request up to the bounded timeout without freezing unrelated coroutines, MCP callers, or health checks on the event loop. Where fcntl is unavailable, the portable fallback (_portable_lock) uses O_CREAT | O_EXCL atomic file creation — guaranteed exclusive-create semantics on every supported filesystem — bounded by the same kind of timeout and offloaded through the same client boundary.

docs.title: Path Canonicalization
docs.text:
Every fencing guarantee above depends on the cache key, the generation fence, invalidate_path(), and the outbound request all agreeing on the same request path. NetBoxApiClient.build_url() resolves ./.. path segments via urljoin() before a request hits the wire, so a request through an unnormalized-but-equivalent alias (e.g. /api/dcim/../ipam/prefixes/5/) still lands on the canonical resource (/api/ipam/prefixes/5/) on the wire. _normalize_request_path() performs the identical dot-segment resolution and is called once, at the very top of _request_impl(), before any cache-related computation — so the cache key, the generation snapshot, and every invalidate_path() call downstream are always keyed to the same canonical path the request actually used, never the literal alias text. Without this, a write issued through such an alias would mutate the canonical resource while invalidating cache entries for the never-cached alias path, leaving the canonical cached entries (which a normal read would hit) stale and servable. netbox_mcp/models.py's CallInput._validate_path() independently rejects decoded ./.. segments outright at the MCP tool boundary, so a raw nbx-mcp call always targets exactly the resource its path spells out.

Dot-segment resolution alone is not enough: aiohttp builds the actual outbound request via yarl.URL(str) (the default, encoded=False), which percent-decodes every RFC 3986 unreserved character (ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "." / "_" / "~") across the whole URL — not only literal or percent-encoded dot segments — before resolving any resulting ./.. segments. So aliases with no dot segment at all, such as /api/%64cim/device%73/5/ (%64 decodes to d, %73 decodes to s), also resolve to /api/dcim/devices/5/ on the wire. _normalize_request_path() reproduces this by canonicalizing through yarl.URL(f"http://netbox-sdk.invalid{normalized}").raw_path — after, not instead of, the existing posixpath.normpath()-based repeated-slash collapsing, since yarl parsing alone does not collapse // runs (only urljoin(), used later in build_url(), does that). Percent-encoded path separators (%2F and %5C, case-insensitive) are different: NetBox, plugins, and reverse proxies can decode them before route matching even when yarl preserves their encoded spelling on the wire, making the literal cache path ambiguous. _normalize_request_path() therefore rejects them before URL construction, cache access, or network dispatch instead of guessing which deployment layer will split the segment. Other encodings, including unreserved-character aliases and encoded query values passed separately through query, retain their existing behavior. Without these rules, a write through an encoded alias could mutate the canonical resource while invalidating cache entries keyed to different literal text, leaving the canonical cached entry stale and servable by a verification read.

docs.title: Crash-Consistent Cache Commits
docs.text: save() and refresh() register the key in the per-path index before writing the entry file — not the reverse. Each individual write (_write_entry, _write_index_state) is already atomic on its own (temp file + os.replace()), but committing an entry is inherently a two-file operation, and a crash or OSError between the two writes must degrade to a safe outcome. load() only checks whether the entry file exists — it never consults the index — while invalidate_path() only walks keys already registered in the index. Writing the entry first (the order used before this fix) could leave an orphan entry file on disk that load() would happily serve, but that invalidate_path() could never discover to purge on a later write — an invalidation-invisible stale hit servable indefinitely. Registering the index first means the only possible interruption leaves an index key with no matching entry file, which load() already treats as an ordinary cache miss.

docs.title: Crash-Safe Portable Locking
docs.text:
The portable fallback lock (_portable_lock, used on platforms without fcntl, notably Windows) is an O_CREAT | O_EXCL exclusive-create file. Unlike flock(), nothing releases it automatically if the holding process dies — and path_generation() is called unconditionally before every cacheable GET, so an abandoned lock file would otherwise block every future request through that path for the full 30 second timeout, forever, since nothing else ever removes it. Two changes make this crash-safe:

  • Ownership-safe stale-lock reclamation. _portable_lock writes the creating process's PID plus a unique acquisition token into the lock file (while still accepting legacy PID-only files). A waiter checks the PID via _pid_is_alive() (os.kill(pid, 0) on POSIX; OpenProcess/CloseHandle on Windows). Reclaimers for a confirmed-dead owner's exact record serialize through an O_CREAT | O_EXCL claim file keyed to that record, re-read it while holding the claim, and create the replacement lock before releasing the claim. Two waiters that both observed one stale file therefore cannot unlink each other's newly created live replacement. Empty or mid-write records remain ambiguous and are left for the bounded timeout.
  • Graceful, stale-safe degradation on lock-acquisition failure. path_generation() catches TimeoutError and returns the sentinel _LOCK_UNAVAILABLE_GENERATION (-1, which never collides with a real generation since those start at 0 and only increase) instead of propagating the exception, logging a cache_lock_timeout warning. The client treats that sentinel as an explicit cache-bypass state: it skips fresh-HIT lookup, conditional revalidation, and persistence for the request. save() and refresh() also return their in-memory entry unpersisted when their own lock attempt times out. If invalidate_path() times out after a write, it still propagates internally so the existing warning path runs, but it first creates a unique per-path unavailable marker visible to every cache-store instance sharing the root. A later path_generation() must successfully retry the invalidation and remove the markers it observed before it can trust that path again; a newer concurrent timeout creates a different marker and cannot be erased by the older recovery.

docs.title: Fail-Safe Purge on a Corrupted Cache Index
docs.text:
A per-path index file can exist but fail to parse — truncated by a crash mid-write on a filesystem without atomic-rename guarantees, hand-edited, or corrupted by an out-of-band process. _load_index_state_or_none() returns None instead of a degraded empty state when the index file exists but cannot be parsed as valid JSON with the expected shape (still returning (0, []), not None, when the file is simply absent — the ordinary case for a path never previously written). save(), refresh(), path_generation(), and invalidate_path() all read the index through a single shared wrapper, _load_index_state_or_purge(), rather than calling _load_index_state_or_none() directly.

An earlier version of this cache degraded a corrupted index to a safe-looking empty (0, []) state only inside save(), refresh(), and path_generation(), on the reasoning that those three callers only use the index to register or fence new writes. That reasoning missed a race: save() and refresh() don't just fence, they also rewrite the per-path index file — so an ordinary write for one key on a corrupted path would "heal" the on-disk index with a fresh, valid-looking one that had silently forgotten every key the corrupted index still registered. Those forgotten keys' entry files were never purged and became permanently unreachable through the index, yet load() decides hits by entry-file existence alone and never consults the index — so they kept being served as fresh hits indefinitely, surviving even a later invalidate_path() call for that same path, since by then the index no longer listed them to purge.

_load_index_state_or_purge() closes this by giving all four callers the same fail-safe response to a corrupted index: on None from _load_index_state_or_none(), it calls _purge_all_entries(corrupted_index_path) and returns (0, [], purged=True) to the caller.

A subsequent fix closed a second race in that recovery path: the freshly reset generation was always 0, and nothing distinguished it from a real, trustworthy 0 — a GET that captured expected_generation=0 on a path that had never been invalidated could lose a race against a concurrent write bumping the path to generation 1, and if the index was then found corrupted (for any unrelated reason) by the time that GET's save()/refresh() ran, the recovered 0 would match its stale captured value and let the pre-write response persist with a fresh TTL, hiding the committed mutation. _load_index_state_or_purge() now also calls _mark_path_unavailable(path) as part of recovery, and every caller (save(), refresh(), path_generation()) checks the purged flag and treats it exactly like a lock-timeout outage — save()/refresh() return their in-memory entry/refreshed-entry unpersisted, and path_generation() returns _LOCK_UNAVAILABLE_GENERATION — instead of trusting the reset 0 as a fence value. invalidate_path() does not need this check: it always writes a fresh, incremented generation regardless of purged, and the marker _load_index_state_or_purge() just set self-heals on the very next path_generation() call for that path via the existing lock-timeout bypass-and-clear flow.

An earlier version of _purge_all_entries() deleted every *.json file store-wide unconditionally — every entry file and every other path's index file, not only the corrupted path's own — reasoning that the generation-fencing invariant above made a whole-store reset safe from any of the four call sites. That reasoning missed a race of its own: resetting an unrelated, healthy path's generation back to 0 could let an in-flight GET for that path, which had captured generation 0 before losing a race against that path's own concurrent write bumping it to 1, have its now-stale save() pass the fence anyway — the rewound 0 is indistinguishable from the pre-write value the GET originally captured — and resurrect data the write had already invalidated.

_purge_all_entries(corrupted_index_path) now recovers only the corrupted path (plus any other index file that independently fails to parse mid-scan): it builds a known_keys set from every other, still-parseable idx-*.json index (leaving those indexes' own generations and entries completely untouched), deletes corrupted_index_path itself, and unlinks only entry files not listed by any surviving healthy index. Since save()/refresh() always register a key in its index before writing the entry file, an entry can only be unlisted by every valid index if the index that used to list it is the one being recovered from — so this scan can never mistakenly drop a healthy path's entry.

Secondary corrupted indexes need an additional safeguard. The scan knows only their on-disk names (idx-<digest>.json), not their plaintext request paths, so deleting them outright would turn a previously invalidated generation into an ordinary missing index interpreted as generation 0. _purge_all_entries() now extracts the digest and publishes an unavailable-<digest>-*.marker before removing each secondary corrupted index. The index filename and marker prefix use the same SHA-256 of the request path, so later path-based checks discover that marker without reversing the hash. load(..., path=path), save(), and refresh() reject the marked path; path_generation() completes invalidate_path() and advances the replacement index before clearing the marker. If the marker cannot be persisted, the corrupted index remains in place as the sentinel instead of being converted into a trustable missing index.

The whole scan-and-delete pass still runs under the same _global_guard_path() lock save(), refresh(), and invalidate_path() take around their own index-then-entry write pair, so it stays serialized against a concurrent writer for a different, healthy path the same way the original locking fix intended: that writer either finishes its whole index+entry pair before a purge can start, or only starts writing after the purge has already finished. The lock is acquired only around each method's actual write section, never around the read-then-decide phase that discovers the corruption and calls _purge_all_entries() in the first place — holding it there would have the corrupted path's own call deadlock against itself when it reaches its own write phase.

docs.title: Textual Composition Pattern
docs.text: netbox-sdk uses a React-style composition pattern for Textual UI work: build screens from small reusable widgets, pass configuration through constructor arguments, and compose behavior by nesting widgets instead of building deep inheritance trees.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• keeps layout readable in compose()
  • makes theme and styling rules reusable
  • lets small widgets evolve independently
  • reduces fragile base-class coupling
  • maps well to NetBox's own Python-side UI composition model

docs.title: Core Rule
docs.text:
Prefer composition over inheritance for UI structure.

Use inheritance when:

  • extending a Textual primitive with a narrow, reusable behavior such as NbxButton
  • creating a self-contained stateful widget with a clear public API

Prefer composition when:

  • assembling headers, bodies, toolbars, and content regions
  • sharing visual structure across multiple screens
  • expressing "slots" such as header/body/footer areas

docs.title: React Mapping
docs.text:
React pattern:

<Panel>
  <PanelHeader title="Object Attributes" subtitle="NetBox detail-style panel" />
  <PanelBody>
    <Status />
    <Table />
    <Trace />
  </PanelBody>
</Panel>

Textual pattern in this repo:

class ObjectAttributesPanel(Vertical):
    def compose(self):
        yield NbxPanelHeader("Object Attributes", "NetBox detail-style panel")
        with NbxPanelBody(id="detail_panel_body"):
            yield Static("Ready", id="detail_status")
            yield DataTable(id="detail_table")
            yield Static("Cable Trace", id="detail_trace_title", classes="hidden")
            yield Static("", id="detail_trace", classes="hidden")

docs.title: Standard Building Blocks
docs.text:
Current shared composition primitives live in netbox_tui/widgets.py:

Primitive Role NbxButton Themed button with tone, size, chrome semantic props NbxPanelHeader Panel title bar NbxPanelBody Panel content container with optional tone / surface ContextBreadcrumb Clickable topbar breadcrumb with scoped dropdown menus; emits CrumbSelected / MenuOptionSelected SupportModal Self-contained ModalScreen shared by main and dev TUIs; inherits active theme via CSS class on mount

These should be the default starting point for new reusable UI pieces.

docs.title: 1. Compose screens from leaf widgets
docs.text:
Keep App.compose() focused on arranging major regions.

  • app shell
  • top bar
  • sidebar
  • main workspace
  • overlays

Move repeated subtrees into dedicated widgets once they have meaning.

docs.title: 2. Treat constructor args like React props
docs.text:
Widget inputs should be explicit and semantic.

Good:

NbxButton("Send", size="medium", tone="primary")
NbxButton("Close", size="small", tone="error")
NbxPanelHeader("Object Attributes", "NetBox detail-style panel", tone="primary")
NbxPanelBody(surface="background")

Avoid passing styling intent indirectly through ad-hoc class strings when a semantic argument would be clearer.

docs.title: 2.1 Theme values should also be props
docs.text:
Theme-aware reusable widgets should receive semantic styling inputs through constructor arguments, similar to React props.

Preferred:

NbxButton("Send", size="medium", tone="primary")
NbxPanelHeader("Danger Zone", tone="error")
NbxPanelBody(surface="panel")

Avoid:

Button("Send", classes="custom-primary custom-medium")
Static("Danger Zone", classes="red-header")

Use semantic props such as:

  • size
  • tone
  • surface
  • chrome

Theme-aware composition also includes surface propagation. If a reusable widget mounts nested Textual primitives internally, the parent widget must carry semantic theme intent down to those children and verify the final rendered surfaces.

Important examples:

  • modal widgets must theme the dialog container and action buttons, not only the ModalScreen
  • tabbed widgets must theme TabbedContent, ContentTabs, ContentSwitcher, and the active TabPane
  • editor/list widgets must theme both their outer container and the framework-owned inner parts that paint backgrounds in focus or ANSI paths

docs.title: 3. Use nested widgets as slots
docs.text:
When a widget has recognizable regions, model them as child widgets instead of one large monolith.

  • header
  • body
  • footer
  • toolbar
  • empty state

docs.title: 4. Keep public methods behavior-focused
docs.text:
A composed widget should expose intent-level methods such as:

  • set_loading()
  • set_object()
  • set_trace()

Avoid leaking internal child structure unless the caller truly owns that structure.

docs.title: 5. Keep styling in TCSS
docs.text:
Composition defines structure. TCSS defines appearance.

  • use semantic classes on reusable widgets
  • keep theme logic in TCSS and theme JSON
  • avoid runtime color decisions in widget constructors

Exception:

  • when Textual runtime defaults still override the selected theme in terminal-only paths such as ANSI-mode Screen / ModalScreen or mounted internal subwidgets, add a narrow runtime surface sync in the owning widget or app
  • if you take this escape hatch, also document the reason in the relevant theme/design docs and keep the runtime override limited to semantic theme tokens

Practical rule:

  • first fix the theme palette if the structural tokens themselves are wrong
  • then fix recursive TCSS selectors for framework-owned internals
  • only then add runtime surface syncing for the specific widgets that still escape the theme contract

docs.title: 6. Keep inheritance shallow
docs.text:
Do not create long widget inheritance chains for layout reuse.

Preferred:

  • ObjectAttributesPanel(Vertical) composed from NbxPanelHeader and NbxPanelBody

Avoid:

  • BasePanel -> PanelCard -> DetailPanel -> ObjectAttributesPanel -> SpecializedPanel

docs.title: Project-Wide Standard
docs.text:
For new Textual work in netbox-sdk:

  1. Start with composition.
  2. Pass theme/styling intent as semantic props on reusable widgets.
  3. Extract reusable visual primitives into netbox_tui/widgets.py.
  4. Document new primitives in contributor docs if they become project-standard.
  5. Only add inheritance when the widget is truly a behavior-specialized primitive.
